div.head: I Cn 22.6
div.ab: Ne he ne byð wel Cristen, þe þæt geleornian nele, ne he nah mid rihte oðres mannes to onfonne æt fulluhte ne æt bisceopes handa þe ma, ær he hit geleornige, þæt he hit wel cunne.
Ne he ne bið wel Cristen, ðe þæt geleornian nyle, ne he nah mid rihte oðres mannes to onfonne æt fulluhte ne æt bisceopes hánda ðe má, ær he hit geleornige, þæt he hit wel cunne.
Þe he ne bið well Cristen, þe þæt geleornian nolde, ne he nah mid rihte oðres mannes to onfonne æt fulluhte ne æt-biscopes handa þe má, ær he hit geleornge, þæt he hit wel cunne.

nec uere Christianus habendus est, qui non uult eam discere; nec ad eum iuste pertinet aliquem in sancto baptismo suscipere nec a manibus episcopi in confirmatione et datione Spiritus sancti, antequam discat, ut bene sciat eam.
Quinimmo non bene Christianus est, qui hec di[s]cere neglexerit; nec debet rite alium ad fontem baptismatis suscipere neque ad manus impositionem episcopi uenire, donec ea bene didiscerit.
Ne he ne bið wel Cristen ðe þæt geleornian nyle, ne he nah mid rihte oðres mannes to onfonne æt fulluhte ne æt bisceopes hánda ðe má, ær he hit geleornige þæt he hit wel cunne.
Ne he ne byð wel Cristen þe þæt geleornian nele, ne he nah mid rihte oðres mannes to onfonne æt fulluhte, ne æt bisceopes handa þe ma, ær he hit geleornige þæt he hit wel cunne.

Auch (Desshalb A) ist der nicht recht Christ, wer das nicht lernen will (wollte A), noch darf er gesetzlich jemanden zur Taufe [als Gevatter] und ebenso wenig aus des Bischofs Hand [als Firmelpathe] empfangen, bevor er jenes [beides] lernt, dass er es gut kann.

Nor (Therefore, A) is he truly a Christian who will (would, A) not learn it, nor may he lawfully receive anyone [as godparent] at baptism, or any more from the bishop's hand [as sponsor at confirmation], before he learns it so that he knows it well.
He is not a true Christian who refuses to learn it, nor may he lawfully stand sponsor to another man at baptism, and as little at confirmation, until he learns it and knows it well.
That person who refuses to learn it is not a good Christian, nor can he legitimately sponsor another at baptism, much less at confirmation, until he learns it so that he knows it well.
div.note: Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G; BR: added from Gesetze I p. 305, October 2026 (MS Cons)
at confirmation: Literally, “at the bishop’s hand.”
